title: Pal-Awda plans protest against Israeli real estate event in Brooklyn
seoTitle: Brooklyn protest against real estate event

tea.why: Protesters oppose an Israeli real estate event being held at a local business, alleging it facilitates the sale of land in the West Bank.
tea.want: The group demands an end to sales of property in Israeli settlements and opposes the use of local businesses for such events.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Organizers announced the protest will take place at 7:00 p.m. outside the Essen NY Deli in Midwood.

summary: The Palestine Right to Return Coalition (Pal-Awda) has scheduled a protest for November 25, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. outside the Essen NY Deli in the Midwood neighborhood of Brooklyn. The demonstration targets an event hosted by the brokerage firm CapitIL. Pal-Awda stated that they are protesting against the sale of land in the West Bank, which they describe as stolen Palestinian land. The City College of New York chapter of Students for Justice in Palestine also expressed opposition to the event. A representative for CapitIL stated that the firm is not promoting real estate in Judea and Samaria during this event. Local officials and community members have expressed concerns regarding security, while some have encouraged public support for the deli. The NYPD and Shomrim have reportedly offered assistance to maintain safety in the area.
organizers: Students for Justice in Palestine (City College of New York chapter)
demands: Stop sales of land in West Bank settlements
End use of local businesses for Israeli real estate events
response: A representative for CapitIL stated the firm affirms the right to protest. New York City Council member Inna Vernikov criticized the protesters, and Elan Kornblum of Great Kosher Restaurants noted that the NYPD and Shomrim have offered assistance to keep the area safe.

arrests.text: at least six arrests at Pal-Awda-affiliated demonstrations targeting Israeli real estate events in 2025 and 2026

updates.text: Reports indicated Pal-Awda scheduled a protest for Wednesday in Brooklyn following the dismantling of a specialized NYPD unit.
Organizers confirmed the protest location as the Essen NY Deli in Midwood and reiterated their opposition to the real estate event.
